steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Source analysis is a core skill in OCR J198, especially in the Depth Study paper

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Always consider three elements: content (what it says), provenance (who wrote it, when, why), and context (what else was happening)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ancient sources include writers like Herodotus, Thucydides, Livy, Polybius and Plutarch

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ancient sources may be biased, incomplete, or written long after events — always note their limitations

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What three elements should you always consider when analysing a source? | Q: Why can a biased source still be useful? | Q: What is the difference between reliability and utility?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Content (what it says), provenance (who wrote it, when, why), and context (what else was happening at the time). | Because bias itself reveals attitudes, values and perspectives of the author or their society, which can be valuable evidence. | Reliability concerns whether a source is accurate and trustworthy; utility concerns how useful it is for answering a specific question — a source can be useful even if unreliable.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Start source answers by identifying the source's provenance — who, when, why Use the formula: 'This source is useful because... However, it is limited because...' for utility questions Always support your points about a source with specific evidence from the source itself For highest marks, cross-reference the source with your own knowledge Remember that asking 'what does this source NOT tell me?' is just as important as what it does
